summary: Independent exact-byte acceptance of the uncommitted M0 Flight Readiness review surface. Both required aggregates were recomputed with a reviewer-written implementation before any semantic work and again immediately before this verdict, and matched exactly both times: 36 files at sha256:7a860b03...4324d and 59 files at sha256:9eea3014...b19a. Five of five frozen input bindings matched by direct hashing. The full recorded battery was re-executed and extended: eight PYTHONHASHSEED values instead of five, four working directories instead of three, an independent rebuild into a temp directory that produced byte-identical fixture payloads, and a runtime spy confirming seven genuine evaluate_flight invocations returning real FlightReadinessPacket objects. A reviewer-written DOM suite executing the real unmodified app.js passed 21 of 22 assertions covering receipt reach, the eligibility gate, typed absence, four fail-closed paths, read-only model stability across 35 route-views, and prohibited authority; its one failure, assertion G, surfaced NB-1 and revealed no read-only violation. All twelve PNG captures were opened and read directly, closing the package's third recorded Coverage Gap, which no prior session could attest to. WCAG contrast was recomputed independently and reproduced the claimed 4.76:1 floor and 15.83:1 ceiling. 37 checks run, 36 passed, 1 failed as written by the reviewer, 0 skipped; every check belonging to the package passed. Four non-blocking English-record findings, no blocking findings. The result remains a local fixture-only, read-only, pre-P3 prototype and nothing broader.

tests_failed_detail: The single failure is one of the reviewer's own assertions, not an artifact check. Every check belonging to the package passed: bindings, fixtures, determinism, both node syntax checks, the behaviour suite, the overflow measurements and all three mechanical suite runs. Reviewer assertion G demanded that no <form>, <input>, <textarea> or <select> appear anywhere across 35 route-views; it failed because the Checks route renders three view-filter controls. That failure is the finding recorded as NB-1. It did not reveal a read-only violation and the verdict does not turn on it, but it failed and is counted as failed rather than folded into a clean number.

non_blocking_findings: NB-1: evidence-receipt.md section 6 states 'there is no form and no data-entry control', but the Checks route renders two <select> view filters and one <input type=checkbox>, each label-associated. No <form>, no text entry, no submit; all three are view filters carrying the on-screen disclosure 'View filter only - no packet, check, evidence or source state changes', and the model is byte-identical after 35 navigations. The sentence understates the control inventory in the safe direction and contradicts the same document's own filter paragraph; README.md states it correctly.

NB-2: evidence-receipt.md section 6 attributes the lower row-ink density of receipts-narrow to 'the receipts route being shorter at 390px'. Direct visual inspection shows the actual cause is a five-column receipt table that scrolls horizontally inside its own container, leaving a wide empty right region per row at 390px. The observation was correctly logged as an observation rather than a defect, but the explanation was supplied without the capability to see it.

NB-3: Coverage Gap 5 understates its own consequence. It records that the fifth route tab is off-screen below roughly 620px with keyboard arrow navigation still reaching it. Direct inspection of boundaries-narrow.png shows that when the fifth route is the active one the tablist displays no selected tab at all, so at 390px there is no visible indication of which route is displayed.

NB-4: evidence-receipt.md states twelve WCAG foreground/background pairs were measured; modelling the palette as actually used yields fourteen pairs. Both stated bounds, 4.76:1 and 15.83:1, reproduce exactly.
